blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: TRAI was established under the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India Act, 1997, to regulate telecommunication services in India.
The TRAI (Amendment) Act of 2000 bifurcated powers by creating the Telecom Disputes Settlement and Appellate Tribunal (TDSAT) to handle adjudicatory functions.
TRAI makes recommendations to the Central Government regarding license terms, introduction of new service providers, and spectrum management.
It fixes and regulates tariffs for telecommunication services and ensures quality of service (QoS) for consumers.
In 2004, the Central Government notified broadcasting and cable services under the ambit of TRAI's regulatory functions.

blocks.content: The main objective of TRAI is to provide a fair and transparent policy environment which promotes a level playing field and facilitates fair competition.

rows: Adjudicatory tribunal for dispute resolution and appeals
Laying down QoS standards and regulating tariffs
Hearing disputes between licensor, licensee, service providers, and consumers

items: TRAI's recommendations are advisory in nature and not binding on the Central Government.
Dispute settlement functions between service providers and consumers or government are handled by TDSAT, not TRAI.
TRAI regulates tariffs and quality of service standards for both Telecom and Broadcasting sectors.
